transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. [Name]... I'm here because of my eating. I've been having these nights where I just eat and eat. And then... I just sit there. With all the crumbs and the empty containers around me. And I feel so ashamed. Just disgusted with myself, honestly. It gets so bad that the next morning, I can hardly bring myself to pray. I can't even look folks at church in the eye. I just can't keep living like this.
After one of these episodes of eating a large amount, do you ever try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot?

No, I don't do anything like that. I've never tried to make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or anything. And, well, at my age I'm certainly not out there exercising to burn it off. I just... I just sit there with a full stomach. I usually just go to bed feeling heavy and sick about what I just did.
Over the past three months, about how often would you say these overeating episodes have been happening—roughly how many times per week?

Well, ever since my friend passed... I'd say these late-night eating spells have been happening at least once or twice most weeks. And there really hasn't been a month where they let up at all. It's just been going on like that steadily.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent episodes of eating large quantities of food (binge eating) occurring at least once or twice weekly, persisting steadily for at least three months, associated with marked subjective distress, shame, and guilt. There is no evidence of compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, or excessive exercise, ruling out bulimia nervosa (F50.2). The absence of purging or compensatory behavior combined with regular, distressing binge episodes fits the pattern of Binge Eating Disorder, which is coded under ICD-10 as F50.8 (Other eating disorders), since ICD-10 lacks a distinct BED code.
